name: Motion/state memory used to select or gate appearance comparison in trackers (SAMURAI 2024 motion-aware memory selection; HiM2SAM 2025; Samba/SambaMOTR ICLR 2025; TrackSSM 2024)

'SAMURAI: Adapting Segment Anything Model for Zero-Shot Visual Tracking with Motion-Aware Memory'. arXiv:2411.11922 v2 (30 Nov 2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.11922 ; code https://github.com/yangchris11/samurai (opened, see full_text_checked). full_text_checked: SAMURAI: arXiv HTML v2 read (Sec. 4.1 motion modeling, Sec. 4.2 memory selection, Tables 1-6); code read: sam2/sam2/modeling/sam2_base.py (constructor defaults, Kalman logic in _forward_sam_heads, memory selection loop in _prepare_memory_conditioned_features) and sam2/sam2/configs/samurai/sam2.1_hiera_l.yaml (threshold values). HiM2SAM: arXiv HTML v3 read (memory design, point tracker, Table 4 ablation, main and attribute tables); repository README read, source files NOT opened; numeric thresholds/memory sizes not given in the text. Samba: arXiv HTML v1 read (architecture, MaskObs, training recipe, test tables, Table 4 and placement/occlusion ablations, hard-sequence table); appendix details on losses and parameter count not found; code not opened. TrackSSM: arXiv abstract page and HTML v2 read (method, Tables IV-VII, main results); code not opened.
inputs_state_output: SAMURAI / HiM2SAM (single-object VOT): strong frozen base = SAM 2.1 (Hiera image encoder, memory attention over a bank of past mask-memories, 3 candidate masks with predicted IoU and object score). Added weak cue = linear Kalman filter on the box of the chosen mask (centre, w, h + velocities). Two roles: (a) late score fusion for mask choice: score = 0.15*KF-IoU + 0.85*SAM-IoU (code kf_score_weight 0.15), KF used only after 15 stable frames with IoU > 0.3; (b) memory gate: a past frame enters the 7-slot memory (num_maskmem 7) only if SAM mask IoU > 0.5, object-score logit > 0.0 and KF-IoU > 0.0; scan backward up to 16 pointers, the immediately previous frame always kept. Output = mask/box per frame. HiM2SAM adds: CoTracker3 point tracking only when combined confidence < tau (thresholds not given), memory split into short-term FIFO of high-confidence frames and long-term memory of frames where the chosen mask is far (directed Hausdorff) from alternative proposals, i.e. frames where a distractor existed and was resolved. Samba / SambaMOTR (MOT, tracking-by-propagation): Deformable DETR R50 decoder gives track embeddings; each tracklet has its own selective SSM (Mamba-style) hidden state updated by its embedding + sine-cosine box encoding; states of all tracklets are synchronized by self-attention + FFN (posterior placement); output = residual update of the track query Q_{t+1}=Q_t+dQ; newborn tracks start with zero state; MaskObs: observations with confidence <= 0.5 are not fed to the state, so the state evolves from its own history and neighbours. TrackSSM (MOT): no appearance; input 5-frame history of (xc,yc,w,h,dx,dy,dw,dh); Mamba encoder -> flow feature; 6-layer Flow-SSM decoder predicts next box; replaces the Kalman filter in ByteTrack (IoU association). Ours: frozen MASA-R50 RoIAlign embedding per real detection region, cosines to snapped exemplar, tagged previous target, and an UNCONDITIONAL accumulated bank (EMA alpha 0.5 over every tagged previous target, scripts/z13_hybrid_identity_20261026.py appearance()), + 32 PCA products; FlyVis 68 regional features from a bounded grey eye crop, recurrent over exemplar+search frames; two-stage readout (identity -> full-box transfer gate). Mapping: the SAMURAI/HiM2SAM mechanism corresponds to gating WHICH tagged past targets enter our bank (our bank currently has no gate); Samba corresponds to replacing the bank by a per-track learned recurrent state that can skip uncertain observations and see neighbours.
fusion_and_training: SAMURAI and HiM2SAM: completely training-free; base frozen; motion enters (i) as late weighted score fusion with a small fixed weight alpha_kf=0.15 (chosen on LaSOT test itself, Table 4; 0.5 is worse than 0.15), and (ii) as a hard threshold gate on memory insertion. The weak cue cannot damage the base much because its weight is small and the gate only removes memory frames (worst case: fewer memories). No mechanism prevents ignoring it - it is hand-weighted. Code detail: the KF memory threshold is 0.0 (any overlap) and the object-score threshold 0.0, so the memory gate is driven mainly by the base's own mask-IoU confidence (> 0.5); the motion part of 'motion-aware memory' rejects only frames whose mask does not overlap the KF prediction at all. Samba: end-to-end joint training of detector decoder + SSM + sync (AdamW 2e-4, 10-frame clips, gradients on last 5 frames, 8 RTX 4090); residual query update (direct prediction 64.2 vs residual 67.2 HOTA) is the safeguard against damaging the base query; MaskObs is the observation gate. TrackSSM: motion model trained alone (Smooth L1 + GIoU, step-by-step linear pseudo-labels), then plugged into a fixed ByteTrack association.
labels_and_loss: SAMURAI/HiM2SAM: no labels, no loss (zero-shot). Samba: MOTR-style set-based detection/tracking losses with identity carried by query propagation [uncertain: exact losses not stated in the HTML read]; hard negatives handled implicitly through query competition and the synchronization attention between tracklets; no explicit neighbour-pair sampling. TrackSSM: box regression only (Smooth L1, GIoU on SportsMOT), pseudo-labels by linear interpolation between consecutive positions (S2L); no identity labels. None of the four uses explicit hard-negative mining among similar neighbours; none trains a gate on 'was this memory frame correct'.
data_camera_resolution_rate: SAMURAI/HiM2SAM: single-object long-term tracking benchmarks LaSOT (1400 videos, test 280, avg ~2500 frames, 30 fps), LaSOT_ext (150 videos), GOT-10k, TrackingNet, NFS, OTB100; moving cameras common; per-attribute labels incl. illumination variation, full/partial occlusion, background clutter, fast motion, camera motion; no MOT, no BDD100K. Samba: DanceTrack (100 videos, uniform appearance dancers, non-linear motion), BFT (birds), SportsMOT; input short side 800, max 1536. TrackSSM: MOT17 (near-linear pedestrians), DanceTrack, SportsMOT; YOLOX-x detections; BDD100K only cited, no results. None uses night/glare driving video like our BDD100K subset.
metrics_and_numbers: SAMURAI (arXiv 2411.11922 v2): Table 3 LaSOT AUC with SAM2.1-L base: none 68.32; +motion 70.81; +memory selection 72.67; both 74.23 (Pnorm 76.16/78.87/80.67/82.69). Table 4 alpha_kf: 0.00 -> 72.67, 0.15 -> 74.23, 0.25 -> 73.76, 0.50 -> 72.92 (text says 0.2 best and Pnorm 82.60 - internal inconsistencies). Table 1 SAMURAI-L LaSOT 74.2, LaSOT_ext 61.0, GOT-10k AO 81.7. Table 5 gains vs SAM2.1: LaSOT AUC +4.68 (B), +5.69 (L); LaSOT_ext +1.97 (B), +2.48 (L). Table 6 attributes LaSOT AUC SAM2.1-B -> SAMURAI-B: fast motion 56.1 -> 62.5, full occlusion 57.6 -> 63.0, partial occlusion 64.6 -> 69.1, background clutter 67.7 -> 73.1; LaSOT_ext L: illumination variation -3.5% (the only non-improving attribute), camera motion +16.5%. HiM2SAM (arXiv 2507.07603 v3) Table 4 LaSOT SAM2.1-L: point tracker only 73.73 (+165.95 ms); long-term memory only 73.71 (+0.39 ms); KF+PT+SM 74.85; all 75.09. Main: LaSOT 75.1, LaSOT_ext 62.8 (SAMURAI-L 74.2 / 61.0). Attributes vs SAMURAI (base): partial occlusion +2.6, full occlusion +1.8, background clutter +2.4, illumination variation +1.3, out-of-view +0.7. Samba (arXiv 2410.01806 v1) Table 4 DanceTrack TEST: SSM only 63.5 HOTA / 53.8 AssA; +MaskObs 64.8 / 54.3; +Sync 65.9 / 55.6; +longer training 67.2 / 57.5; MeMOTR 63.4 / 52.3; MOTR 54.2 / 40.2. Sync placement: none 66.0, prior 66.1, posterior 67.2. Occlusion handling: freeze 65.9 HOTA / 56.6 AssA vs MaskObs 67.2 / 57.5. Six hardest DanceTrack sequences: HOTA 40.9 -> 44.5, AssA 25.1 -> 28.3 with sync. Test: DanceTrack 67.2 HOTA, BFT 69.6, SportsMOT 69.8 (MeMOTR 68.8). TrackSSM (arXiv 2409.00487 v2) Table IV val HOTA Kalman vs TrackSSM: MOT17 75.0 vs 74.9; DanceTrack 47.1 vs 53.8; SportsMOT 67.8 vs 81.2. Table V history length 3/5/10/20/40: DanceTrack 53.9/53.8/52.5/52.9/53.9. Table VII S2L: DanceTrack 51.4 -> 53.8. Test: MOT17 61.4 (ByteTrack 63.1, i.e. worse), DanceTrack 57.7, SportsMOT 74.4; 5.1M parameters. These are the authors' metrics; they must not be translated into expected HOTA or offline utility on our bench.
distinguishing_ablations: SAMURAI Table 3 is the cleanest 2x2: memory gating alone over the frozen base +4.35 LaSOT AUC, motion score fusion alone +2.49, both +5.91 - single run, single benchmark, hyperparameter alpha chosen on the same test set, no seeds or CI. It does NOT isolate the motion part of the memory gate: with KF threshold 0.0 in code, the memory-only row is essentially confidence-gating by SAM's own IoU (> 0.5) plus a 'nonzero overlap with KF prediction' check; no row 'memory gated by confidence only' vs 'by confidence + motion' exists. Nor is there an equal-capacity non-informative control (e.g. random frame selection with the same number of memories). Negative/weak signals: illumination variation does not improve (-3.5% LaSOT_ext L) - directly relevant to our dark/glare regime; alpha_kf 0.5 almost erases the gain (72.92 vs 72.67) - too much weight on the weak cue hurts. HiM2SAM: long-term distractor-aware memory alone +5.39 over base but only +0.24 on top of KF+PT+SM - mostly redundant once confidence gating exists; first three rows reused from SAMURAI (not independent). Samba: per-tracklet SSM memory alone (63.5) is equal to MeMOTR's EMA-like long-term memory (63.4) - the state-space memory per se adds nothing over an EMA memory of comparable role; the gains come from MaskObs (+1.3, skipping uncertain observations = a gate) and synchronization among tracklets (+1.1; 66.0 -> 67.2 in the placement study); all on DanceTrack test, single runs. TrackSSM: learned SSM motion equals Kalman on near-linear MOT17 (74.9 vs 75.0) and is worse on MOT17 test than ByteTrack; large gains only with non-linear motion (DanceTrack, SportsMOT); history length barely matters (52.5-53.9). No source compares a bio-inspired or pixel-motion recurrent state against a generic SSM of equal size.
explanations_addressed: (a) Fly features carry no unique identity information beyond appearance: not addressed directly; design analogy only - in SAMURAI motion does not add identity information to SAM features, it decides which appearance memories are trusted; this suggests a role for FlyVis that does not require unique identity information, only information about memory reliability (occlusion, overlap, abrupt change). (b) Information exists but fusion ignores it: caution/design analogy - SAMURAI avoids learning entirely (fixed small weight + hard gate), so the weak cue cannot be ignored; Table 4 shows the useful weight is small (0.15) and large weight hurts. (c) Saved readout features lost it: not addressed. (d) FlyVis lacks lobula/identity pathway: not addressed (none biological). (e) Motion helps only in subsets diluted by averaging: direct evidence that gains concentrate in attributes (fast motion +11.4%, full occlusion +9.4%, clutter +8.0% relative) and Samba's hardest sequences (+3.6 HOTA vs +1.2 overall); and that illumination variation is NOT helped - caution for darkness/glare. (f) Ceiling too low (+2.8 pp perfect identity vs +2 pp): not addressed by these sources; but it bounds a memory gate even more tightly - a gate can only fix errors caused by a contaminated bank, a subset of identity errors, so its ceiling is below +2.8 pp and must be measured with an oracle-clean bank first.
evidence_strength: Moderate-to-weak for our question. SAMURAI: preprint, very widely reused, official code verified (thresholds read from code), but a single benchmark ablation without seeds/CI, hyperparameters chosen on test, internal text/table inconsistencies, HiM2SAM reuses its ablation numbers (not an independent confirmation). Samba: peer-reviewed ICLR 2025, single-run ablations on DanceTrack test, code not verified here. TrackSSM: preprint, code public but not opened; its Kalman-equal result on MOT17 is the relevant (negative) piece. None tests motion-gated memory in MOT over a frozen ReID appearance, none in darkness/glare, none with BDD100K.
difference_from_tried: Genuinely different in role: everything tried so far ADDS fly features as columns to the identity classifier next to MASA cosines (concatenation into gradient boosting, neighbour-relative features, T4/T5 motion consistency, tagged previous target, unconditional bank). The memory-gate mechanism instead keeps the appearance comparison and changes WHICH past appearances form the reference: our bank is an unconditional EMA (alpha 0.5) over every tagged previous target, with no quality, occlusion or motion gate; the snapped exemplar is fixed. A gated bank (insert tagged region only if reliable) and a 'distractor-resolved' long-term memory (HiM2SAM) have not been tried. A per-track learned recurrent state over embeddings (Samba) has not been tried either; our nearest is the EMA bank. Partly similar: the T4/T5 motion-consistency features already encode motion agreement, but as classifier inputs, not as a gate on memory insertion.
math_precheck: All CPU on the saved fit104 / train26 query tables (MASA region embeddings, tagged regions, previous_query links, truth identity labels, FlyVis 68 regional features), no core training. Step 0 (target size): for each query compute whether the tagged previous target used to build the bank was the TRUE target (truth labels); count bank contamination rate and, among appearance-only identity errors (MASA identity model picks wrong region or misses), the fraction occurring on tracks whose bank/previous tag was contaminated. Step 1 (oracle ceiling of any gate): rebuild the bank with an ORACLE gate (insert only tagged regions that are truly the target), recompute bank cosines, refit the same appearance-only identity model with nested folds, and compute offline utility with the existing readout gate. Gain_oracle = utility(oracle-gated bank) - utility(current bank), paired bootstrap over videos. Also report the upper bound obtained by giving each region the max cosine over the oracle-clean history (best-memory oracle). Step 2 (gate predictability): train a small gate classifier p(tagged region is true target | features available at insertion time) with three feature sets: (i) no-fly cues: detection confidence, IoU between tag and Kalman/velocity prediction, max IoU with neighbour detections (overlap/occlusion), MASA cosine of tag to previous bank, box size change; (ii) eye input R1 statistics of the same crop; (iii) FlyVis D/C regional features of the tagged region (T4/T5 activity, neighbour means). Measure AUC/average precision of contamination detection per set and the conditional gain of (iii) over (i) (log-loss gain with nested folds, as in C03). Step 3: plug each predicted gate (thresholded or soft weight in the EMA) into the bank and measure utility, three-way: current bank / gated bank without fly / gated bank with fly. Decision rules (record before running): STOP the memory-gate line if Gain_oracle upper CI < +0.5 pp (or point < +0.3 pp) on fit104 - a perfect gate cannot matter, so neither can FlyVis; STOP the FLY role if the fly gate does not beat the no-fly gate in contamination AP with CI excluding 0 or its utility over the no-fly gated bank has CI including 0 on train26; only if Gain_oracle >= +0.5 pp and the fly gate captures a material share of it beyond the no-fly gate (e.g. >= 30% of Gain_oracle) consider new FlyVis activity or a state readout on GPU. Expectation stated honestly: with same-track cosine 0.955 vs 0.103 for different objects and EMA alpha 0.5, a few contaminated insertions are diluted quickly, so Gain_oracle may well be near 0; this step costs minutes and decides the line.
cue_role_and_regime: Role: memory selector/gate (which tagged past appearances enter the bank or long-term memory), optionally a soft weight in the EMA; secondary: small-weight late score fusion (SAMURAI alpha 0.15). Not a new identity feature. Regime targeted: bank contamination after occlusion, crossing paths and box swaps between similar neighbours (the moment the previous tag jumped to a neighbour), fast motion and clutter; HiM2SAM's long-term memory targets frames with a resolved distractor. Darkness/glare: SAMURAI shows no gain on illumination variation, so no support there; the motion gate does not repair low-quality appearance, it only avoids storing it.
no_fly_equivalent_control: Cheapest equal-role controls: (1) SAMURAI-style hand gate with no learning: insert tag only if detection score and Kalman-IoU of the tag with the predicted box exceed thresholds and no neighbour overlaps it above an IoU threshold (all from saved geometry); (2) confidence-only gate (the base's own identity probability > threshold) - this isolates the 'motion' part, which SAMURAI never did; (3) learned gate with the same gradient boosting on no-fly geometry + eye input R1 statistics; (4) for the Samba-like variant: a GRU/SSM over the sequence of MASA tag embeddings + box encoding with the same parameter count as the fly readout, with MaskObs-style skipping of low-confidence observations; (5) a random gate with the same insertion rate (non-informative control). FlyVis counts only if (fly gate) > (best of 1-4) on train26 with paired bootstrap CI excluding 0.
bio_node_mapping: Memory gating by motion consistency loosely corresponds to a recurrent/state node of the fly pathway: T4/T5 direction-selective motion as the evidence, and downstream facilitation/persistence along a trajectory (STMD/CSTMD1-like facilitation, lobula LC/LPLC object cells) as the 'trust this observation' signal; FlyVis itself models the optic lobe up to T4/T5 and 34 output types with internal recurrent dynamics, but no explicit memory-gating neuron. Connectome for lobula LC/LPLC exists in FlyWire 783 (data/flywire/783 in the project). The SSM memory of Samba has no biological counterpart.
novelty_overlap: Nearest prior: SAMURAI/HiM2SAM (Kalman-gated memory over frozen SAM2) and Samba (gated per-track SSM memory); ours would differ by using a connectome-constrained fly-vision state from the pixel crop as the gate over a frozen ReID bank in MOT - novelty modest, only meaningful if it beats a Kalman/confidence gate.
candidate_node_change: Node: FlyVis readout/state - add a 'memory-trust' output (readout of FlyVis activity of the tagged region at insertion time, optionally integrated over frames as a leaky state) that gates insertion of MASA tag embeddings into the bank (hard threshold or soft EMA weight), instead of feeding FlyVis activity as identity columns. It addresses the FlyVis problem that its saved activity adds no unique identity information over appearance: the gate needs information about observation reliability (occlusion, swap, abrupt motion), where pixel motion could in principle be informative. Version 1 (CPU, saved features): gradient-boosting gate on FlyVis D regional features of the tag. Version 2 (only if justified): leaky recurrent state over FlyVis outputs along the track (facilitation-like). Controls with equal capacity: appearance only with current unconditional bank; appearance + oracle-clean bank (ceiling); appearance + no-fly gate (Kalman/neighbour-overlap/confidence); appearance + eye-input R1 gate; appearance + stock C gate; appearance + random gate of equal insertion rate; for version 2, a GRU of equal size over the same inputs. Condition to proceed to GPU (new FlyVis activity or core fine-tuning on contamination labels): Gain_oracle >= +0.5 pp with CI excluding 0 on fit104, fly gate beats the best no-fly gate on the pre-registered train26 check (CI excluding 0), and the gated-bank utility moves the total identity utility toward the +2 pp criterion; otherwise record as negative and do not train.
strongest_objection: The memory-gate gain in SAMURAI is not shown to come from motion: in the official code the Kalman memory threshold is 0.0 and the gate is dominated by SAM2's own mask-IoU confidence, the ablation has no confidence-only row, hyperparameters were tuned on the test set, and HiM2SAM's 'confirmation' re-uses the same numbers. In our bench appearance is already near-separable (cosine 0.955 vs 0.103) and the bank is an EMA that dilutes contamination, so the oracle ceiling of any gate may be tiny compared with the +2.8 pp perfect-identity ceiling; and even if a gate helps, a Kalman/neighbour-overlap gate (no fly) is the natural winner on near-linear rigid-vehicle motion (TrackSSM: learned motion = Kalman on MOT17), leaving no FlyVis result. Darkness/glare (illumination) is exactly the attribute where SAMURAI shows no gain.
cost_and_hardware: Steps 0-3 of the precheck: CPU only, saved MASA embeddings, tags, truth labels and FlyVis features; roughly tens of minutes to a few hours with nested folds and bootstrap [uncertain: depends on refitting cost of the existing readout]. No GPU. A leaky-state version over saved per-frame FlyVis outputs is also CPU. Only new FlyVis activity maps (state readout on all frames of a track) or core fine-tuning on contamination labels would need the 12 GB GPU and author approval.
